sanskrit: tatra saṃsthāpite liṃge svayaṃ devena śaṃbhunā | yatpātitaṃ purā liṃgaṃ vālakhilyairmaharṣibhiḥ || 5 || atikopasamāyuktaiḥ kasmiṃścitkāraṇāṃtare | tadā devena pratijñātaṃ sarveṣāṃ tridivaukasām || 6 || acale tu mayātraiva sthātavyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ | tataḥ kālena mahatā vasatastasya tatra ca || 7 ||
english: 4-7. Once upon a time when the gods after appeasing Lord Śiva, who usually mounts upon a bull, asked him to remain ever present in the Arbuda mountain, the radiant God himself proceeded to put up there. On his own he founded his worshipable Liṅga there. But that worshipable Liṅga was brought down by the great sage Vālakhilya. The Sage had done so due to excess anger for some reason. Then Lord Śiva made a promise before all gods saying that he would not move out of there under any circumstances and would stay there beyond any doubt. Since then and in the unchangeable march of great Time he has been present there.

There is nothing which cannot be given to you.

english: 49-51. One who plays on a musical instrument shall obtain the benefit of the Vājapeya sacrifice. The dancer shall obtain the benefit arising from taking a plunge in all the Tīrthas. The person who gives money to these people shall obtain all these merits. By listening to or by seeing (these) one obtains one-sixth of the benefit. If a person is in difficulties and he cannot obtain water anywhere, or if a person is afflicted with sickness, he should perform the Mārjana (‘wiping off’) rite by taking (i.e. muttering the) name of Viṣṇu.
